subject: Nanotechnology
title: Buckyballs Change Everything
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Buckyballs Change Everything.

hook.text: In 1985, scientists vaporized graphite with a laser and found a perfect soccer-ball molecule.

buildup.text: Sixty carbon atoms in pentagons and hexagons — they named it buckminsterfullerene, or C60.

discovery.text: Buckyballs proved carbon could form closed cages — a shape nobody predicted from theory alone.

twist.text: The discovery opened the floodgates — nanotubes, graphene, and carbon dots all followed.

climax.text: The discoverers won the 1996 Nobel Prize for revealing an entirely new form of carbon.

punchline.text: A soccer ball made of carbon launched a revolution.

quiz.question: What is a buckyball (C60)?
options: A cage-shaped molecule of 60 carbon atoms
